title: O wrapper do orquestrador congela modelo e effort no argv: project.toml nao governa nenhuma sessao alem da primeira
description:
Medido ao vivo em 2026-07-26 por inspecao de processo, nao por leitura de codigo. O wrapper do orquestrador (pid 16261) foi iniciado em Mon Jul 13 09:27 e seu argv contem literalmente: while true; do claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions --session-id "$sid" --model 'opus' --agent subagent-orchestrator "$(cat .claude/.cam-orchestrator-prompt.txt)". O commit a8aa5ac5 de 2026-07-25 20:16 (model routing: fable orchestrator/planner, max effort orch, opus reviewer/auditor) alterou scripts/cam/project.toml para orchestrator igual a fable e efforts.orchestrator igual a max, ou seja doze dias DEPOIS do wrapper nascer. O processo vivo do orquestrador (pid 30534, filho do wrapper) roda com --model opus ate agora.

Dois parametros divergem simultaneamente: (1) o modelo, que o toml declara fable e o processo executa opus; (2) o effort, que o toml declara max e que simplesmente NAO APARECE no argv, nem como --effort nem em qualquer outra forma. O reviewer despachado no mesmo periodo (pid 86024) recebe --model opus corretamente porque e resolvido por dispatch a cada spawn, o que isola o defeito no caminho do orquestrador.

A parte grave nao e o valor errado, e a persistencia: o argv esta congelado dentro do corpo do laco while true do bash -c, portanto o auto-respawn pos-cycle-close (CAM-23 e CAM-162, watcher SIGTERM mais respawn pelo wrapper) reexecuta o MESMO argv literal. A sessao atual e resultado de um respawn ocorrido apos o fechamento do ciclo CAM-406 e mesmo assim carrega opus. Consequencia: a configuracao de modelo e effort do orquestrador so tem efeito na primeira sessao apos um cam run, e nenhuma edicao de project.toml, nem qualquer numero de respawns, a atualiza. Para um produto cuja premissa e configuracao declarativa em TOML, isso e quebra de contrato.

Agravante de observabilidade: a divergencia e silenciosa. Nada no event log denuncia que o processo vivo diverge da configuracao declarada, tanto que o handoff de cycle-close do CAM-406 registrou orchestrator igual a fable como decisao aplicada enquanto a sessao inteira executou opus, e o defeito so apareceu porque o operador estranhou a indicacao de modelo na interface. Qualquer relato de custo ou desempenho por modelo produzido ate aqui esta atribuido ao modelo errado.

Direcao proposta, a validar na spec: o wrapper deve RE-RESOLVER modelo e effort a cada iteracao do laco, lendo scripts/cam/project.toml no momento do respawn, em vez de interpolar o valor uma unica vez na construcao do argv. Assim uma edicao de configuracao passa a valer no proximo respawn sem exigir reinicio de cam run. Pontos a decidir na spec, sem escolher antecipadamente: se a releitura ocorre no wrapper em shell ou se o wrapper passa a invocar um resolvedor deterministico do proprio binario; como o effort e propagado, dado que ele hoje nao chega ao argv de forma alguma e portanto precisa ser tratado como funcionalidade ausente e nao apenas desatualizada; e se uma divergencia entre configuracao declarada e processo vivo deve emitir evento observavel, dado que o modo de falha real foi ser silenciosa.

Requisitos de nao-regressao: o session-id precisa continuar estavel entre respawns, o contador n com teto max igual a 5 precisa continuar limitando respawns consecutivos, a entrega do handoff via CAM_ORCH_REHYDRATE precisa continuar funcionando, e a escrita de .claude/.cam-orch-pid precisa continuar apontando para o pid do wrapper. Criterio de aceitacao central: com cam run em execucao, alterar o modelo do orquestrador em project.toml e disparar um respawn deve produzir um processo com o novo modelo, comprovado por inspecao de argv do processo vivo e nao por leitura de codigo.

spec.scope: Make the orchestrator wrapper re-resolve BOTH model and effort at every respawn, and emit --effort at all (today it is never emitted by any code path). Two distinct defects share one fix site. Defect 1, stale model: resolvePhaseModel runs exactly once per cam run, in setupPanes (src/commands/run.ts:486-495), and its result is interpolated as a plain JS string into the bash -c payload at run.ts:274 (const model = opts.model ?? DEFAULTS.orchestrator) and run.ts:287 (--model ${q(model)}). The while-true loop body at run.ts:286-326 re-execs that identical literal line on every respawn, so the parent cam run process is never re-entered and no edit to project.toml can ever take effect without a full cam run restart. Defect 2, absent effort: readPhaseEffort (src/config/models.ts:197-212) has ZERO production consumers repo-wide; it is referenced only by its own definition and by tests (test/config/models.test.ts, test/commands/config-persist.test.ts). [efforts] orchestrator is therefore dead config, fully parsed, fully unit-tested, fully green, and wired to nothing. The claude CLI does accept --effort <level> with tiers low, medium, high, xhigh, max, and the repo's EFFORT_OPTIONS (src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx:124-130) already matches that set exactly, so no new validation layer is required. DIRECTION DECIDED (the issue deferred this to the spec): re-resolution must invoke a deterministic resolver from the cam binary, NOT a bash-side TOML re-read. A shell re-read would be a second implementation of resolvePhaseModel and would fork CAM-398's nested [models.codex] pin rule, flat-pin policy, models_cache auto-resolve and claude typo-guard into bash. The binary resolver keeps one source of truth and dissolves the issue's observability question for free, because the existing emitter (src/logging/spawn-resolution.ts) can then fire on every respawn instead of only once at cam run (run.ts:508-523). Mirror the in-repo precedent: reviewer, implementer, planner and auditor all already re-resolve per dispatch (src/supervisor/review.ts:394,404-409 with the explicit comment at review.ts:379-381 'Re-resolve per-call, not once at construction'; src/supervisor/loop.ts:1108,1118-1122; src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:655,658 and 731,734). The orchestrator is the sole outlier. IN SCOPE: run.ts wrapper construction, the resolver entry point it calls, wiring readPhaseEffort to an argv, a configPath seam at the run.ts resolution site, per-respawn spawn-resolution events, and updating the existing wrapper tests. OUT OF SCOPE: the persona frontmatter effort channel (src/templates/frontmatter.ts), the worker-phase dispatch sites (already correct), and the CAM-420 supervisor test isolation work.
acceptanceCriteria: ORACLE (must be red against main): an integration test builds the wrapper, then changes the orchestrator model in a staged project.toml BETWEEN the initial build and a simulated respawn, runs the real assembled bash with a stub claude on PATH that appends its own argv to a file once per invocation, and asserts the SECOND recorded invocation carries the NEW model while the FIRST carries the old one. Following the existing real-bash pattern at test/commands/run.test.ts:19-69 and the real-tmux pattern at test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts:160-169. A test that only asserts --model is present in a built string does NOT satisfy this criterion.

ORACLE (must be red against main): the orchestrator claude invocation carries --effort <level> whose value comes from readPhaseEffort('orchestrator'), and the level is one of low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Red against main because the literal --effort appears nowhere in src/, test/, templates/ or scripts/ argv builders today.

ORACLE (must be red against main): effort re-resolves per respawn under the same mechanism as model, proven by the same before/after staged-config test as criterion 1, asserting the second invocation's --effort differs from the first when the staged config changed between them.

readPhaseEffort (src/config/models.ts:197) has at least one production consumer reachable from the orchestrator spawn path. Verifiable by grep: references to readPhaseEffort outside src/config/models.ts and outside test/ must be non-empty.

The resolution site that run.ts uses accepts an injectable configPath, mirroring the CAM-405 seam at src/supervisor/review.ts:373,394,407, and every NEW test added by this issue resolves against a staged temp config rather than the live scripts/cam/project.toml.

ASYMMETRIC FAILURE HANDLING, both halves asserted by test: (a) at initial cam run, a not-ok model resolution still aborts before any pane is respawned, preserving the existing { blocked: true, message: 'model-resolution-failed: ...' } contract at run.ts:492-494 UNCHANGED; (b) at respawn, a failed resolution must NOT prevent the orchestrator from coming up. It falls back to the last known-good value, respawns anyway, and emits an observable event recording the divergence. Rationale: no operator is present at respawn, so failing closed there would let a config typo silently brick the autonomous loop, which is strictly worse than the defect being fixed.

A spawn-resolution event is emitted on every respawn, not only once at cam run. Today emitSpawnResolution fires exactly once (run.ts:508-523), which is why the CAM-406 cycle-close handoff recorded orchestrator=fable as an applied decision while the live session executed opus with nothing in the event log contradicting it.

NON-REGRESSION, each asserted: the respawn counter n with cap max=5 still bounds consecutive respawns and still resets to 0 on reason cycle-close (run.ts:310); CAM_ORCH_REHYDRATE is still exported pointing at the .consumed.json path after the mv and before the uuid mint (run.ts:294,300,305); .claude/.cam-orch-pid still receives the WRAPPER bash pid via printf '%s' "$$" before the loop starts (run.ts:285); --permission-mode bypassPermissions and --agent subagent-orchestrator are still present and unchanged; and the session id is still RE-MINTED as a fresh lowercased uuid on every respawn (run.ts:305-306). See gotcha 1: the issue text asserts the opposite about session id and is wrong.
bun run check:all passes green (typecheck, biome lint with --error-on-warnings, and the full test suite).
gotchas: FACTUAL ERROR IN THE ISSUE TEXT, do not encode it: CAM-425's non-regression list states 'o session-id precisa continuar estavel entre respawns'. That is false. run.ts:305-306 mints a FRESH lowercased uuid on every respawn (sid=$(uuidgen | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')) and rewrites .cam-orch-session. What is actually stable across respawns is the wrapper bash pid in .cam-orch-pid (run.ts:285). Preserve the real behavior (fresh uuid per respawn). Do NOT change the wrapper to hold the session id stable. This is the same class of spec error that escalated the CAM-398 plan through two audit rounds.

Do NOT reimplement model resolution in bash. resolvePhaseModel (src/config/model-resolution.ts:145) carries CAM-398's nested [models.codex] pin rule, the flat non-claude-shaped pin acceptance policy, models_cache.json auto-resolve, and the claude alias typo-guard. A shell-side TOML read would fork all of it and would silently diverge on the next model-resolution change.

CAM-405/CAM-420 LIVE-CONFIG HAZARD IS PRESENT AT THIS EXACT SITE: run.ts:486 (readBackend()) and run.ts:487-491 (resolvePhaseModel) pass NO configPath, so they read scripts/cam/project.toml resolved from process.cwd(). Two existing tests deliberately depend on the live repo config: test/commands/run-model-resolution.test.ts:315-342 and test/commands/run-codex-auth.test.ts:257. The suite header at run-model-resolution.test.ts:36-39 admits the hazard in writing. Add the seam rather than staging a cwd for every new test.

test/commands/run-model-argv.test.ts:21-51 is NOT a valid oracle for this issue. All four of its tests pass a literal model into buildOrchestratorPaneCommand and assert it appears in the output. They pass today and would still pass after a no-op change, because they prove the argv contains a model, never that the model is current at respawn time.

test/run.test.ts:574-707 asserts the exact string shape and internal ordering of the loop body (flag order, mv before export, jq before mv, pid write before 'while true; do', no trailing & on the claude line, teardown ordering). Restructuring the loop WILL break several of these. Update them to assert the new correct shape. Do NOT weaken or delete assertions to make them pass.

The wrapper must locate the cam binary robustly. It runs as bash -c under tmux with an inherited environment, the binary lives at ~/.local/bin/cam, and it may be absent or mid-rebuild at the moment a respawn fires (in-place rebuilds are routine in this repo). A resolver invocation that fails, hangs or is not found must fall through to the last known-good value and still respawn, per acceptance criterion 6b.

There is a SECOND effort channel that this issue does not own: the persona frontmatter (src/templates/frontmatter.ts:57-92), written only by a cam config wizard save (src/commands/config.ts:158-171). It is currently STALE, .claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md:4 reads effort: xhigh while project.toml reads max, because commit a8aa5ac5 touched only project.toml. State in the implementation that argv is the runtime authority, but do not delete or rewire the frontmatter channel here.

--effort tiers are exactly low, medium, high, xhigh, max (confirmed against claude --help on the live CLI). src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx:124-130 and EFFORT_DEFAULTS (src/config/models.ts:81-87, orchestrator: 'xhigh') already match that set, so no new validation or typo-guard layer is warranted. Note EFFORT_DEFAULTS.orchestrator is 'xhigh' while the live project.toml declares 'max'; the config value must win.

A second, unrelated orchestrator spawn path exists at src/commands/setup.ts:476-481 (the onboarding handoff) and passes neither --model nor --session-id. It is out of scope; do not conflate its while-true keyboard menu (setup.ts:486) with the respawn loop.

buildOrchestratorPaneCommand has exactly one production call site, run.ts:497, so the signature is free to change. It is documented as pure string assembly with no I/O (run.ts:259-270); if resolution now needs I/O, keep the pure builder pure and inject the resolved values or the resolver command string, so the unit tests at test/run.test.ts:574-707 stay synchronous.

Project invariants: Bun only (Bun.spawn / Bun.$ / Bun.file, never node:child_process), TypeScript strict with noUncheckedIndexedAccess so array and regex-group access is T | undefined and must be guarded, and no --permission-mode flag may be added to any subcommand.
domainTerms: argv freeze: a spawn parameter interpolated once into the wrapper's bash -c payload at cam run time, so it is a fixed literal inside the loop body and cannot change for the life of the wrapper process regardless of how many respawns occur.

respawn: one iteration of the wrapper's while-true loop after the claude child exits, driven by the presence of the handoff marker and bounded by the counter n against cap max, distinct from a cam run restart which is the only thing that re-enters the TypeScript parent.

fail-closed vs fail-safe: fail-closed aborts before spawning when resolution fails and is correct at cam run where an operator is watching; fail-safe falls back to the last known-good value and spawns anyway, and is correct at respawn where no operator is present and refusing to spawn would brick the autonomous loop.

spawn resolution event: the observability record written to .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl by src/logging/spawn-resolution.ts carrying { phase, model, backend }, currently emitted exactly once per cam run, which is why a live process diverging from declared config produces no signal.
